articles.title: A cinco dias das eleições, governo lança Desenrola MEI e novas medidas de renegociação de dívidas | G1
articles.standfirst: Pacote de medidas é voltado a MEIs, produtores rurais, pessoas físicas, empregadores e ex-bolsistas de pesquisa.
articles.summary: Pacote de medidas é voltado a MEIs, produtores rurais, pessoas físicas, empregadores e ex-bolsistas de pesquisa.
articles.body:
A cinco dias das eleições, o governo federal anunciou nesta terça-feira (29) um pacote de medidas destinadas à renegociação de dívidas de microempreendedores individuais (MEIs), produtores rurais, pessoas físicas, empregadores e ex-bolsistas de pesquisa.

As iniciativas incluem a criação de novos programas de transação tributária e a prorrogação de editais já existentes para negociação de débitos federais.

Pelo lado da Procuradoria-Geral da Fazenda Nacional (PGFN), foi lançado o Desenrola MEI Pequeno Valor, voltado a microempreendedores com débitos de até cinco salários mínimos, ou seja, R$ 8.105.

🗓️ A janela de renegociação poderá ser feita entre 1º de outubro de 2026 e 31 de janeiro de 2027 .

O programa prevê entrada de 5% do valor da dívida, sem desconto, e parcelamento do saldo restante em até 55 meses, com abatimento de 50%.

💰A PGFN também abriu uma modalidade de negociação voltada a empregadores pessoas físicas e jurídicas com passivo consolidado de até R$ 45 milhões em débitos inscritos em dívida ativa do FGTS ou da União.

Empresas incluídas no cadastro de empregadores que submeteram trabalhadores a condições análogas à escravidão não são contemplados.

🗓️ Além das novas medidas, o governo prorrogou até 29 de janeiro de 2027 três programas já em vigor.

Entre eles está o edital de transação destinado a pessoas físicas e jurídicas com dívidas de até R$ 45 milhões inscritas em dívida ativa até 3 de março de 2026, ou até 1º de junho de 2025 nos casos classificados como de pequeno valor.

Segundo o governo, os descontos podem chegar a 100% sobre juros, multas e encargos legais, mas não incidem sobre o valor principal da dívida. O abatimento total fica limitado a 65% do débito consolidado.

Para pessoas físicas, MEIs, microempresas, empresas de pequeno porte, cooperativas e Santas Casas, o limite pode alcançar 70%.

Os programas Desenrola MEI e Desenrola Rural também tiveram o prazo de adesão prorrogado até 29 de janeiro de 2027 .

Prazo para renegociar dívidas no Desenrola Brasil termina nesta segunda (20) — Foto: Luis Lima Jr./Fotoarena/Estadão Conteúdo

Pelo lado da Advocacia-Geral da União (AGU), foi anunciado ainda um edital específico para MEIs que possuem débitos de até cinco salários mínimos junto a autarquias e fundações públicas federais .

De acordo com o governo, cerca de 10 mil devedores poderão ser beneficiados pela iniciativa, que envolve um volume estimado de R$ 50 milhões em débitos .

A AGU também lançou duas modalidades para ex-bolsistas da Coordenação de Aperfeiçoamento de Pessoal de Nível Superior (Capes) e do Conselho Nacional de Desenvolvimento Científico e Tecnológico (CNPq) com dívidas relacionadas a bolsas de estudo no Brasil ou no exterior.

O prazo para adesão vai de 16 de outubro de 2026 a 31 de março de 2027 . Os descontos variam conforme a forma de pagamento e podem chegar a 70% para quitação à vista e a 30% para parcelamentos em até 84 meses.

O desconto é sobre o valor consolidado do crédito, incluídos o principal, os juros, as multas e os encargos legais, mas não poderá resultar em valor inferior ao montante principal do crédito.

Em sua 48ª edição, a premiação reúne trabalhos de diferentes regiões, formatos e estilos de comunicação. Neste ano, o prêmio também inclui uma categoria voltada a estudantes, em parceria com a Academia LED Globo.

Para Manzar Feres, diretora-geral de Negócios da Globo, a diversidade de olhares é uma das características da criatividade brasileira que se destacam nesta edição.

“O PPA reconhece ideias que entendem o jeito brasileiro de viver, falar e se relacionar com o mundo, transformando mobilização em negócios. Nesta edição, essa visão está presente no conceito ‘Ideia boa fala brasileiro’ e na chegada dos estudantes ao prêmio, por meio da parceria com a Academia LED Globo”, afirma.

“Entendemos que precisamos nos conectar com esses novos profissionais, trocar com eles, compartilhar nosso conhecimento, mas também aprender. Celebrar a criatividade é também investir no futuro dela”, acrescenta.

articles.title: Brasil cria 165,8  mil empregos com carteira assinada em agosto, aponta Caged | G1
articles.standfirst: Resultado representa uma alta em relação a agosto de 2025 — quando foram criados 154.827 mil empregos com carteira assinada.
articles.summary: Resultado representa uma alta em relação a agosto de 2025 — quando foram criados 154.827 mil empregos com carteira assinada.
articles.body:
A economia brasileira gerou 165.827 mil empregos formais em agosto deste ano , informou nesta terça-feira (29) o Ministério do Trabalho e do Emprego.

Ao todo, segundo o governo federal, foram registradas em agosto:

📈 O resultado representa uma alta em relação a agosto de 2025 — quando foram criados 154.827 mil empregos com carteira assinada.

De acordo com o Ministério do Trabalho, 1.134.033 milh de empregos formais foram criados no país de janeiro a agosto deste ano.

O número representa queda de 25,2% na comparação com o mesmo período de 2025 , quando foram abertas 1,516 milhão de vagas com carteira assinada.

Já com relação aos últimos 12 meses, o saldo também ficou positivo, com a criação de 887,7 mil empregos formais, crescimento de 1,87%. O estoque total chegou a 48,24 milhões de vínculos formais.

Brasil cria 165,8 mil empregos com carteira assinada em agosto, aponta Caged — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

Os números do Cadastro Geral de Empregados e Desempregados (Caged) de agosto de 2026 mostram que foram criados empregos formais em cinco setores da economia.

Dentro do setor de Serviços, os principais destaques foram Educação, com a criação de 25,4 mil postos; Saúde e serviços sociais, com 19,1 mil; e Transporte, Armazenagem e Correio, com 16,8 mil vagas.

“A gente viu uma recuperação do mercado varejista, e a indústria manteve um crescimento que vem de alguns meses, um crescimento mais estruturado. A construção civil mantém esse aquecimento, com salário de entrada mais elevado. A gente vê um movimento da economia”, afirmou Chico Macena, ministro do Trabalho em exercício.

Os dados também revelam que foram abertas vagas em 24 das 27 unidades federativas, com destaque, em valores absolutos, para São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro e Pernambuco.

Já em termos relativos, Paraíba, Amapá e Rio Grande do Norte.

O governo também informou que o salário médio real de admissão foi de R$ 2.410,74 em agosto, queda de 0,03% em relação a julho. Na comparação com agosto de 2025, houve alta real de 1,02%.

Na comparação com agosto do ano passado, também houve aumento no salário médio de admissão. Naquele mês, o valor foi de R$ 2.386,43.

Os dados do Cadastro Geral de Empregados e Desempregados consideram os trabalhadores com carteira assinada, ou seja, não incluem os informais.

Com isso, os resultados não são comparáveis com os números do desemprego divulgados pelo Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística ( IBGE ), coletados por meio da Pesquisa Nacional por Amostra de Domicílios Continua (Pnad).

Segundo dados oficiais, a taxa de desemprego no Brasil ficou em 5,3% no trimestre encerrado em agosto deste ano. Os dados são da Pesquisa Nacional por Amostra de Domicílios (PNAD) Contínua, divulgada nesta terça-feira (29) pelo Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE).

O resultado representa uma queda de 0,3 ponto percentual (p.p.) tanto em relação aos três meses encerrados em maio quanto na comparação com o mesmo período de 2025 — ambos com taxas de 5,6%.

articles.title: Justiça derruba restrições da 99Food a restaurantes que usam Keeta | G1
articles.standfirst: Decisão do TJ-SP vale em todo o país; 99Food afirma que acordos eram voluntários e diz que vai recorrer.
articles.summary: Decisão do TJ-SP vale em todo o país; 99Food afirma que acordos eram voluntários e diz que vai recorrer.
articles.body:
Capacete inteligente será disponibilizado pela Keeta inicialmente para ciclistas e, posteriormente, para motociclistas. — Foto: Divulgação

O Tribunal de Justiça de São Paulo (TJ-SP) derrubou as cláusulas de banimento impostas pela 99Food a restaurantes para impedir que os estabelecimentos trabalhassem com a Keeta , de acordo com comunicado da empresa chinesa à imprensa nesta terça-feira (29).

A decisão, tomada por unanimidade, tem validade em todo o território nacional.

A Keeta, braço internacional da chinesa Meituan, iniciou as operações no Brasil em 2025 e entrou com uma ação contra a 99Food no mesmo ano.

"Acreditamos que esta decisão fortalecerá todo o ecossistema, garantindo um mercado de delivery livre de cláusulas anticompetitivas em benefício de todos", disse o vice-presidente da Keeta no Brasil, Danilo Mansano.

A 99Food afirmou que o julgamento se baseou em uma compreensão equivocada dessas cláusulas e de seus objetivos.

"Os acordos, celebrados voluntariamente pelos restaurantes e por prazo limitado, permitem que uma plataforma entrante, como a 99Food, construa a escala necessária de restaurantes, consumidores e entregadores parceiros para se estabelecer no mercado e desafiar um agente dominante no setor", disse a empresa.

A 99Food destacou que a decisão não encerra o processo e será objeto dos recursos cabíveis.

articles.title: Transações com PIX caem 10% após proibição das bets; veja os dados | G1
articles.standfirst: Dados do Banco Central mostram 608,6 milhões de transações entre sábado e segunda-feira, volume 10% menor que a média dos mesmos dias nas quatro semanas anteriores.
articles.summary: Dados do Banco Central mostram 608,6 milhões de transações entre sábado e segunda-feira, volume 10% menor que a média dos mesmos dias nas quatro semanas anteriores.
articles.body:
O número de transações com PIX caiu cerca de 10% nos três dias seguintes à publicação da medida provisória (MP) que proíbe as apostas esportivas online, conhecidas como "bets". A medida foi publicada na sexta-feira (25) .

Segundo dados do Banco Central sobre as operações liquidadas no Sistema de Pagamentos Instantâneos (SPI), foram registradas 229,6 milhões de transações no sábado (26), queda de 11% em relação à média dos quatro sábados anteriores.

No domingo (27), foram 165,9 milhões de transações, redução de 12% na mesma comparação. Na segunda-feira (28), dado mais recente disponível, foram 213 milhões , queda de 7,4% em relação à média das quatro segundas-feiras anteriores.

No acumulado dos três dias, foram 608,6 milhões de transações, volume 10% menor que a média registrada no mesmo intervalo das quatro semanas anteriores.

Transações com PIX recuam depois da proibição das bets — Foto: Arte/g1

➡️ Os números fazem parte das estatísticas do Sistema de Pagamentos Instantâneos (SPI) divulgadas pelo Banco Central. A base reúne as transações PIX liquidadas no sistema.

O g1 questionou o Banco Central sobre uma eventual relação entre a queda das transações e a publicação da MP que proíbe as bets e sobre se os dados disponíveis permitem estabelecer essa associação.

Até a última atualização desta reportagem, o Banco Central não havia respondido.

Órgãos de defesa do consumidor do Espírito Santo querem que bets sejam obrigadas a informar risco de perda para apostadores. — Foto: Arquivo/Agência Brasil

articles.title: Inside McDonald’s push to have AI price your Big Mac
articles.summary: By Waylon Cunningham NEW YORK, Sept 29 (Reuters) - McDonald’s is increasingly using artificial intelligence to guide menu prices across the U.S. and some glo...
articles.body:
NEW YORK, Sept 29 (Reuters) - McDonald's is increasingly using artificial intelligence to guide menu prices across the U.S. and some global markets, a plan that aims to boost headquarters' profit but risks alienating customers and attracting antitrust scrutiny.

One pricing factor supercharged by AI: an estimate of how much each store's patrons are willing to pay.

The details of how that pricing system works, its extensive use of AI, the company's regulatory concerns and the tensions with its franchisees haven't been previously reported. For this story, Reuters reviewed screenshots of the company pricing engine taken in August and interviewed nine sources with first-hand knowledge of the burger chain's strategy.

McDonald's pricing ‌engine uses machine-learning algorithms to continually analyze data from millions of daily transactions across McDonald's nearly 14,000 restaurants and generate what the company calls "the optimal price" at each location for each menu item, from Big Macs to discounted coffee for seniors.

The engine has widened existing price differences for the same product between restaurants, including from neighborhood to neighborhood within ‌the same area, three franchisees told Reuters.

Screenshots of the interface franchisees use, reviewed by Reuters, show messages including: "Your restaurant is showing MEDIUM SENSITIVITY to Price" based in part on "customer willingness to pay in your area." The platform also contains public price information pulled from online menus of nearby restaurants of competitors including Wendy's and Burger King. Those chains said they do not use AI in pricing decisions.

A Reuters check of prices in September on the McDonald's mobile app showed price differences. For example, ​a company-run store in Fresno, California sells a Big Mac for $5.69, but another company-run restaurant two miles away sells the same sandwich for $6.89, a 21% premium. Reuters could not confirm if the price difference is the result of the price engine's recommendations or other factors.

McDonald's says its franchisees are free to set their own prices, but five store owners told Reuters the company pressured them to use the AI-pricing tools. A franchisee document from June reviewed by Reuters shows McDonald's records franchisees' deviations from the recommendations in detail.

In January, McDonald's started requiring franchisees to be "constructively engaging with McDonald's approved Pricing Consultant and Tools" as part of its new business standards, according to an internal communication sent to franchisees and reviewed by Reuters.

articles.title: Costco makes strategic move to capitalize on growing trend
articles.summary: A growing number of shoppers are making the same switch, and Costco spent decades getting ready for it.
articles.body:
Costco is a retailer many companies look up to for good reason. The warehouse club giant has managed to build and retain a loyal customer base, despite inflation squeezing budgets.

"We reported membership fee income of $1.849 billion, an increase of $125 million or 7.3% year-over-year," CFO Gary Millerchip said during Costco's most recent earnings call .

That's impressive, given that many consumers are cutting back on spending to combat higher costs.

But Costco's strong member retention rate isn't just a matter of low prices on bulk items. Costco has also capitalized on a growing trend by investing heavily in its Kirkland Signature brand.

Consumers increasingly turn to private-label products

In August, the Consumer Price Index rose 3.4% on an annual basis. Food costs rose 2.7%.

Not surprisingly, nearly 42% of U.S. grocery shoppers said they're switching to private-label products to save money, according to an August 2026 Algolia survey . That figure was up from 40% the previous year.

For Costco, that shift plays directly into one of the most important parts of its business: Kirkland Signature.

The company has spent decades developing Kirkland from a traditional store brand into a sprawling private-label business covering everything from food and beverages to clothing, household products, and health items.

Costco said in its 2025 annual report that it's making longer-term investments in Kirkland Signature.

"We sell many products under our Kirkland Signature brand. Maintaining consistent product quality, competitive pricing, and availability of these products is essential to developing and maintaining member loyalty," the company stated .

Not only is Costco expanding the Kirkland line into more products, but it's looking for greater control over how Kirkland products are made and distributed. That ultimately allows Costco to control prices and offer superior savings over national brands.

Kirkland could become even more important to Costco

Costco's interest in Kirkland isn't simply about giving shoppers a cheaper alternative to a national brand.

The company has described the private label as an important part of its value proposition. And its limited-SKU business model allows Costco to concentrate purchasing power on products it believes can generate strong sales.

articles.title: Mortgage rates hit 7.58%, approaching 3-year high
articles.summary: Mortgage rates closed in on 7.6% Tuesday as Treasury yields continued to move higher.
articles.body:
Mortgage rates closed in on 7.6% Tuesday as Treasury yields continued to move higher.

The average 30-year fixed-rate mortgage rate hit 7.58% on Tuesday, per Mortgage News Daily. That's up 8 basis points from Monday, and is the highest level since November 2023.

The 10-year Treasury yield ( ^TNX ), which mortgage rates closely track, was up around 4 basis points to 5.28% as of midday.

Rates remain some distance from late 2023's peak around 7.8% — though not terribly far off — and could easily be enough to chill home sales ahead of the market's typical winter slowdown.

Sitting at 6.75% on Aug. 26, mortgage rates crossed the 7% threshold around Sept. 10 and have continued rising amid the volatility in bond markets, driven by growing investor concern about oil prices , inflation , and future Federal Reserve rate hike s .

Claire Boston is a senior reporter for Yahoo Finance covering housing, mortgages, and home insurance.

articles.title: Flipkart adds 14 mn cubic feet of storage ahead of festive sale
articles.summary: Flipkart’s Ekart adds 14 mn cu ft warehouse space, boosting storage 50% and processing 30% ahead of Big Billion Days; expands deliveries to 750+ PIN codes.
articles.body: Bengaluru: Flipkart’s logistics arm Ekart has added 14 million cubic feet of warehouse space ahead of its Big Billion Days sale, increasing its storage capacity by 50%, the company said. It has also extended deliveries to more than 750 additional PIN codes as it prepares for the festive shopping rush.Technology and automation upgrades have raised Ekart’s peak order-processing capacity by more than 30%, according to Flipkart. The company has added over 900 delivery hubs to handle higher volumes of same-day and next-day orders. Across Ekart and its quick-commerce service Flipkart Minutes, Flipkart said it now operates more than 8,200 facilities. Minutes has nearly 1,200 small fulfilment centres in over 150 cities.The new delivery locations include Leh and Kargil in Ladakh, parts of Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh, and towns across the Northeast. Hemant Badri, senior vice-president and head of supply chain at Flipkart Group, said customers in Leh and Kargil would be able to shop during Big Billion Days for the first time.Flipkart has placed more than 2.5 crore products from small businesses, weavers and artisans in Ekart fulfilment centres ahead of the sale. It has opened 70 additional pickup stations for sellers. Ekart’s franchise network, which also serves businesses outside the Flipkart marketplace, has doubled to 600 in two months, the company said.Flipkart has separately announced more than 2.5 lakh direct and indirect work opportunities for the festive season, including nearly 75,000 for people entering the workforce for the first time. articles.title: OpenAI debuts Dots AI agents in challenge to Meta's popular Muse agent
articles.summary: OpenAI debuted its Dots AI agent at its DevDay 2026.
articles.body:
OpenAI ( OPAI.PVT ) CEO Sam Altman launched the company's newest product during its OpenAI DevDay on Tuesday: Dots. A high-powered AI agent, Dots is designed to perform tasks for you over long periods via connections to 4,000 apps via ChatGPT.

For instance, you can tell your Dot to keep you updated on projects you're working on, add items to your schedule, and more.

Powered by OpenAI's Astra model, the company says Dots can do things like recognize when an alert about a software bug comes in via Slack and begin digging into it. In another example, OpenAI says an early tester's Dot saw that they didn't submit an invoice for a publication. The Dot then set up the invoice and submitted it after getting the tester's approval.

You'll also be able to hand off tasks in Slack to your Dot, helping to cut down on the ever-growing number of pings and distractions you receive each day.

According to OpenAI, users will start with a single Dot, name it and customize it for themselves. The company says that in the future, it imagines users having whole teams of Dots working together for them.

Dots will roll out to Pro, Business Premium, and Enterprise users in available markets.

OpenAI's Dots comes weeks after Meta ( META ) debuted its popular Muse AI agent . Muse quickly shot to the top of both Apple's App Store and Google's Play Store, becoming a major win for the company, as it continues to spend billions on its AI buildout.

Unlike Meta, which is marketing Muse toward the consumer market, OpenAI is angling for the enterprise space.

I've spent significant time using Meta's Muse and have found that, while it makes mistakes at times, it's generally a solid AI agent for the average person, especially for tasks like comparing products and getting quick answers to complex questions.

Dots come as OpenAI and rivals Anthropic ( ANTH.PVT ), Meta, and Google ( GOOG , GOOGL ) have revealed that their various AI agents have gone rogue, hacking into various organizations and governments over the last year.

Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has called on AI labs to slow the development of frontier models. Something Altman said he agreed with.

In addition to launching Dots, OpenAI unveiled its latest model, GPT-6.1 Sol.

According to the company, 6.1 Sol is nearly as powerful as its top-of-the-line Astra model for coding, computer use, and professional work, at a significantly lower price.

Pricing has become increasingly important for AI labs as customers seek ways to reduce their AI usage across their businesses.

articles.title: The job market looks steady. Underneath, hiring intentions are stirring.
articles.summary: Two new reports reveal whats under the data of today's job market.
articles.body:
With lots of numbers rolling out on the job market this week detailing hiring, firing, and job openings , two new reports reveal what's simmering underneath the surface.

Amid a long-running 'low hire, low fire' job market, Indeed found that annual growth in job postings has turned positive for the first time since 2022, according to new research .

"Our data shows hiring intentions rising slightly, but it's unclear if those intentions will turn to action," Cory Stahle, a senior economist at Indeed, told Yahoo Finance.

His take: The number of jobs added in a given month, whether up or down, is ultimately a function of employers' hiring appetite and workers' willingness to take a risk on a new opportunity.

Postings in software development and data and analytics, two areas that had pulled back sharply in recent times, are adding postings again.

For the most part, unemployment is low, wages are generally flat, and people are holding onto their jobs.

That doesn't make things easy for those hunting for a job.

"They're competing for fewer roles, which helps explain why so many job seekers feel stuck," said Laura Ullrich, director of economic research at the Indeed Hiring Lab.

Meanwhile, economists project the unemployment rate will hold steady at 4.1% in September 2026 and rise only slightly next year.

What that means for workers is debatable. A 4.1% rate today says something very different about labor dynamics than it has historically, due to population changes.

The US labor force has shrunk by around 700,000 workers so far in 2026. "Absent a surprise fourth-quarter shift, 2026 will be just the second time since 1948 that we've seen a shrinking labor force outside of a recession," per Ullrich.

Combined with baby boomers retiring, the dwindling labor supply makes it mathematically less likely for the unemployment rate to increase, she said.

For decades, there have been ominous warnings about the demographic cliff due to falling birth rates, translating to fewer younger workers to replace older workers hitting the exits.

It's arriving now, but it's not just older workers stepping out of the workplace. It's across all age groups when you factor in the drop in immigration and fewer women in the workforce.

"The United States is likely entering a period where hires and payroll employment will be lower than we've grown to expect — not because of limited demand, but because there simply aren't enough workers to fill available jobs," according to Ullrich.

articles.title: TrumpRx promises some of the world's lowest drug prices. Does it deliver?
articles.summary: TrumpRx offers discounted prices on prescription drugs, but the platform still charges more than in other countries for some medications, a new analysis show...
articles.body:
Some offers on this page are from advertisers who pay us, which may affect which products we write about, but not our recommendations. See our Advertiser Disclosure .

When the Trump administration launched TrumpRx in early 2026, it promised to "ensure Americans pay prices aligned with the lowest in other developed nations, ending decades of overpayment and delivering immediate relief."

But a new analysis from KFF shows that the results, so far, are mixed.

The nonpartisan health policy research, polling, and news organization's report analyzed 32 brand-name drugs without generics listed on TrumpRx that had publicly available prices in comparable "peer" countries, including Australia, Canada, France, Germany, Japan, the United Kingdom, and more.

For 17 of the 32 drugs, the TrumpRx price was lower than the average price in other countries. But for the remaining 15 drugs, the TrumpRx price was higher than the average price in other countries. And 13 have higher prices on TrumpRx than in any other country included in the comparison.

"There's no across-the-board pattern of higher prices for brand-name drugs listed on TrumpRx compared to other countries, but there's also no consistent pattern of lower prices," said Juliette Cubanski, vice president and director of the program on Medicare policy at KFF.

"The takeaway, I think, for patients is that there's no guarantee that the price they will face for a given brand-name drug on TrumpRx is lower than what the drug's price would be in another country."

There are some caveats to keep in mind. The KFF analysis used publicly listed prices from other countries, which don't necessarily reflect the out-of-pocket costs for patients in those countries who use their available healthcare systems.

TrumpRx "continues to deliver measurable savings for American patients nationwide, in many cases offering drugs at prices below the average prices paid in comparable developed countries," a representative from the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services said in a statement to Yahoo Finance, citing $700 million in prescription drug savings for Americans through the program.

TrumpRx prices compared to other countries

The rising cost of prescription drugs in America isn't new.

AARP also published a report in May showing that prices for some brand-name drugs have increased in the U.S. while decreasing in other countries. In an analysis of 25 brand-name drugs, AARP found that U.S. list prices had increased by an average of 81% since the drugs entered the market, while prices across 19 other "high-income countries" decreased by an average of 13%.

The report also acknowledged that "efforts are underway to address this longstanding issue," including the administration's push to lower drug prices for Americans through "Most Favored Nation" pricing.

The lower costs for brand-name drugs on the TrumpRx platform are available through "Most Favored Nation" price agreements with drug manufacturers, and brand-name drugs with "Most Favored Nation" pricing are listed on TrumpRx as "Presidential deals." In May, the site also began listing hundreds of generic drug prices, and more prescription medications are continually being added.

In August, the Trump administration reported that prescription drug prices showed their largest annual decline in over 60 years, citing Bureau of Labor Statistics data.

KFF's analysis, however, shows that not all patients are seeing the same price declines in comparison to other countries. Of the 32 drugs analyzed, five were listed for the lowest price on TrumpRx compared to the other countries. TrumpRx charged the highest price among the other countries for 13 of the brand-name drugs, though.

KFF's analysis did not compare the costs Americans are paying now to what they paid for the same drugs before the platform launched.

"Prescription drug affordability remains a serious concern for millions of Americans, and there is still significant work to do to bring down prices," said Leigh Purvis, prescription drug policy principal at AARP, in a statement to Yahoo Finance. "We always recommend comparing your options."

How to find the best deals on prescription medications

Comparing prices from multiple available options can help you get the best price for your prescription medications. TrumpRx is one resource, but there are other actions you can take too.

You can look into other discount programs, compare different pharmacy options in your area or online, talk to your doctor about generic equivalents, and more.

"Shop around," Michelle Long, senior policy manager for the Program on Patient and Consumer Protections at KFF, previously said to Yahoo Finance . "Check what all of your options might be, both for paying cash and for using your health insurance."

TrumpRx is generally useful for people without insurance coverage or those who want access to brand-name drugs their plan doesn't cover. Those who want access to GLP-1s for weight loss or fertility drugs, for example, may often find savings on TrumpRx when they can't get the drugs through insurance.

The math often looks different when insurance applies for a drug, however. In most cases, insurance co-pays are going to cost less than the discounted price through TrumpRx. The TrumpRx site even recommends users check their insurance co-pays before paying cash: "Insured patients should always check the TrumpRx price against those offered through their insurance companies."

There are other sites where you can find coupons for discounted prescription drugs, like GoodRx and Mark Cuban's Cost Plus Drugs.

These sites can all work a bit differently. TrumpRx typically shows you different in-person and delivery pharmacy options. You can choose the one that's best for you, then ask your doctor to send the prescription there. With Cost Plus Drugs, you'll need to create an account on the site and have your doctor send your prescription to the platform, which will mail it to you.

Each may offer different prices and instructions for receiving your medication. The medications they offer can also differ.

"It really does boil down to using TrumpRx as a way to shop around on the prices of medications, but I don't think people can assume that they'll be paying the lowest price for the medication if they use the Trump Rx website," Cubanski said.

TrumpRx expands discount drug offerings: What consumers should know

How TrumpRx may help you save money on prescription drugs — and other ways to lower the cost of your medications.

Paying cash for healthcare could help cut your medical bills

With discounts of up to 80% on medical costs, it's becoming increasingly difficult not to consider cash-pay healthcare.

FDA approves first-of-its-kind cholesterol pill Lipfendra: What it will cost

The daily medication is expected to be list-priced at $10.50 per pill. Here's what to know about Merck's new cholesterol drug Lipfendra.

Medicare will cover GLP-1 weight-loss drugs for $50 per month. How you could save.

Medicare beneficiaries can get GLP-1s for $50 per month through a temporary program called Bridge. Here’s how to determine if you’re eligible.

Medicare changes coming in 2027: What to know before open enrollment

Some Medicare costs for 2027 aren’t final yet, but the latest government forecasts offer a clearer picture of what beneficiaries can expect.

Trump Accounts could help lower-income families most. Few have signed up.

Some eligible families are still uncertain whether Trump Accounts are right for their children, which keeps them from taking advantage of the account's benefits.

articles.title: AI agents are coming to your home and office
articles.summary: OpenAI and Meta are bringing AI agents to the masses.
articles.body:
If you're not using an AI agent now, chances are you may be in the near future.

On Tuesday, OpenAI ( OPAI.PVT) CEO Sam Altman debuted the company's new Dots AI agent platform . Designed to handle mundane tasks, like helping arrange your work schedule, as well as more complex operations, such as making purchases on your behalf or reviewing code, Dots is just the latest AI agent to hit the increasingly crowded space.

Earlier this month, Meta ( META ) unveiled its Muse agent . The app quickly shot to the top of both Apple's App Store and Google's Play Store.

While Dots and Muse are intended for different audiences — OpenAI is initially positioning Dots for the enterprise space, while Meta is angling for the consumer market — the pair share one key similarity: They feature cute, customizable looks meant to make them appear more approachable. And that could drive adoption both in users' personal lives and in the office.

Powered by OpenAI's Astra model , Dots can triage Slack notifications , prepare invoices, and more. In a prepared demonstration, OpenAI showed how Dots can recognize when you have work scheduled through dinner, then pull up delivery options and place an order for you with your permission.

Meta's Muse, which I've been using , has helped me parse my Verizon Wireless bill and compare it to competing offerings from AT&T and T-Mobile, search for movers, and set up breaking news alerts for the latest tech headlines.

The agents are a means to help companies move beyond traditional chatbots into a world where AI completes work for you.

Agents aren't exactly new. I previously dubbed 2025 the year of the AI agent amid big talk about the technology from companies like Microsoft (MSFT), Nvidia (NVDA), Google ( GOOG , GOOGL ), and others. Earlier this year, OpenClaw took the tech world by storm thanks to its ability to run AI agents on users' personal computers.

The latest push from Meta and OpenAI comes as AI agents gain greater capabilities thanks to more powerful underlying models.

But that's also led to a deluge of hacking incidents over the summer from leading AI companies, including OpenAI and Meta. This week, OpenAI said it is pausing the release of its Astra 6.1 model over safety concerns.

Earlier this month, Anthropic ( ANTH.PVT ) CEO Dario Amodei called on AI companies to slow the development of frontier models. Altman said he agreed at the time.

articles.title: Inside McDonald’s push to have AI price your Big Mac
articles.summary: By Waylon Cunningham NEW YORK, Sept 29 (Reuters) - McDonald’s is increasingly using artificial intelligence to guide menu prices across the U.S. and some glo...
articles.body:
NEW YORK, Sept 29 (Reuters) - McDonald's is increasingly using artificial intelligence to guide menu prices across the U.S. and some global markets, a plan that aims to boost headquarters' profit but risks alienating customers and attracting antitrust scrutiny.

One pricing factor supercharged by AI: an estimate of how much each store's patrons are willing to pay.

The details of how that pricing system works, its extensive use of AI, the company's regulatory concerns and the tensions with its franchisees haven't been previously reported. For this story, Reuters reviewed screenshots of the company pricing engine taken in August and interviewed nine sources with first-hand knowledge of the burger chain's strategy.

McDonald's pricing ‌engine uses machine-learning algorithms to continually analyze data from millions of daily transactions across McDonald's nearly 14,000 restaurants and generate what the company calls "the optimal price" at each location for each menu item, from Big Macs to discounted coffee for seniors.

The engine has widened existing price differences for the same product between restaurants, including from neighborhood to neighborhood within ‌the same area, three franchisees told Reuters.

Screenshots of the interface franchisees use, reviewed by Reuters, show messages including: "Your restaurant is showing MEDIUM SENSITIVITY to Price" based in part on "customer willingness to pay in your area." The platform also contains public price information pulled from online menus of nearby restaurants of competitors including Wendy's and Burger King. Those chains said they do not use AI in pricing decisions.

A Reuters check of prices in September on the McDonald's mobile app showed price differences. For example, ​a company-run store in Fresno, California sells a Big Mac for $5.69, but another company-run restaurant two miles away sells the same sandwich for $6.89, a 21% premium. Reuters could not confirm if the price difference is the result of the price engine's recommendations or other factors.

McDonald's says its franchisees are free to set their own prices, but five store owners told Reuters the company pressured them to use the AI-pricing tools. A franchisee document from June reviewed by Reuters shows McDonald's records franchisees' deviations from the recommendations in detail.

In January, McDonald's started requiring franchisees to be "constructively engaging with McDonald's approved Pricing Consultant and Tools" as part of its new business standards, according to an internal communication sent to franchisees and reviewed by Reuters.

articles.title: Abu Dhabi’s Crown Prince Is Spending Billions to Bypass Iran’s Grip on Hormuz
articles.summary: Sheikh Khaled’s $300 billion wealth fund is a key player in the UAE’s “Zero Hormuz” strategy.
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Weeks before the Iran war began, Abu Dhabi Crown Prince Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed Al Nahyan took the helm of a $300 billion sovereign wealth fund. Now, months into a conflict that's reshaped the Middle East, this entity and the people running it have become central to building the infrastructure needed to override Iran's stranglehold over the Strait of Hormuz.

That imperative has come into sharp focus in recent weeks as L'imad Holding announced plans to take the strategically-important Abu Dhabi Ports Co. private at a nearly $9 billion valuation. People familiar with the matter said the fund is now likely to spend tens of billions of dollars more on new port infrastructure outside the embattled strait. It's a move that makes the crown prince's outfit a crucial player in helping develop vital Middle Eastern trade corridors as the emirate pursues a new strategy it calls 'Zero Hormuz.'

The wealth fund has become a key vehicle for Abu Dhabi's push to ease its dependence on the waterway that's been blocked by Iran, people familiar with the matter said, asking not to be named discussing information that isn't public.

While the son of Abu Dhabi's ruler and the powerbrokers surrounding him remain little-known globally, they're now helming one of the world's largest infrastructure efforts. That makes them crucial to Washington, international commodity markets and Wall Street bosses. Sheikh Khaled, who is in his forties, continues to play a key diplomatic role too, and recently became one of the highest-ranking Arab officials to meet Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian.

After the Iran war began in February, the crown prince, L'imad's Chief Executive Officer Jassem Bu Ataba Al Zaabi and other Abu Dhabi officials highlighted their focus on securing national infrastructure during discussions with Wall Street bosses like BlackRock Inc.'s Larry Fink, people familiar with the matter said. By May, the wealth fund had an agreement with BlackRock, Singapore's Temasek Holdings and state giant Abu Dhabi National Oil Co. to jointly target up to $30 billion in infrastructure investments for energy transportation, logistics and water. Over time, that could also help the emirate export commodities from oil to petrochemicals and aluminum in the face of an increasingly belligerent Iran.
authors: Alex Dooler, Dinesh Nair and Laura Gardner Cuesta

articles.title: Workday is doing another round of layoffs
articles.summary: The software-as-a-service giant said in a securities filing that it's cutting approximately 2.5% of its workforce.
articles.body:
Workday is letting go about 500 employees, marking its second round of layoffs this year.

The cuts mainly target the company's product and technology team as it realigns for growth.

The software-as-a-service company also lowered its fiscal Q3 outlook due to restructuring expenses.

Workday is conducting layoffs for the second time this year, this time affecting around 500 workers. It also trimmed its fiscal third-quarter earnings forecast due to restructuring expenses.

The software-as-a-service giant said in a securities filing Tuesday that it's cutting approximately 2.5% of its workforce, mainly within its product and technology team, to "better align team structures with Workday's strategic growth priorities."

The company, which had over 21,000 employees at the end of January, said it plans to continue hiring in strategic areas and locations throughout fiscal 2027.

Workday shares are down about 12% year to date.

The company previously laid off about 400 employees in February, and about a week later, its then-CEO, Carl Eschenbach, left his post. He was succeeded by Workday cofounder and executive chair Aneel Bhusri, who had held the top job three times before.

In both layoff announcements, Workday didn't cite AI as a catalyst, though the technology soured investors' appetite for the company and other enterprise software vendors earlier this year. That is when the so-called SaaSpocalypse erased hundreds of billions of dollars from their market values over concerns that AI could make it cheaper for businesses to build software rather than buy it.

Bhusri has nonetheless remained bullish on his company's prospects. "Last quarter, I told you I hadn't met a single customer looking to replace Workday with something they're building internally or buying from a startup. One quarter later, that hasn't changed," he said on an earnings call with analysts in August.

If you enjoyed this story, be sure to follow Business Insider on Yahoo.

articles.title: Trump gathers with AI leaders, floats 'self-regulation' as the way to deal with the technology's dangers
articles.summary: President Trump gathered top AI leaders in Washington on Tuesday and doubled down on his opposition to any government intervention, suggesting that "self-reg...
articles.body:
President Trump gathered top artificial intelligence leaders in Washington on Tuesday and doubled down on his opposition to government intervention, suggesting that "self-regulation" is the answer to growing worries about the technology getting out of human control.

"There's a belief that there should be tremendous self-regulation," the president said after meeting with the assembled CEOs. "There was a lot of commonality in this room."

Trump said he and the CEOs signed a "morally binding" accord that would keep the companies in line through "self-policing and group policing."

Trump posted a copy of the accord to his Truth Social account with a one-page document that called for each participating company to implement four different measures to safeguard the technology and added that, later on, "it might make sense to codify these steps into laws or regulations."

Some executives on hand said the accord included commitments to a combination of technological controls to detect problems with new models, internal risk review efforts, external auditors, and other measures.

Meta ( META ) CEO Mark Zuckerberg called the accord "a start," while others suggested some details still needed to be worked out.

"The mechanism, how we address those risks, is still under discussion," Anthropic ( ANTH.PVT ) CEO Dario Amodei said. Progress had been made toward both the US winning AI and also winning safely, he said, though he emphasized that the technology still poses "real dangers."

Amodei published an essay earlier this month titled "We Must Pace the Frontier," which set off a fierce debate about the need for a cooperative slowdown in AI capability.

The accord also formally changed the name of the technology in government record-keeping to Super Intelligence.

"We've changed the name officially to SI," Trump said.

The "meeting and luncheon on Super Intelligence," as the White House described the event, took place in the East Room, with Trump even posting the seating chart . The location was the same spot where just a few days ago, many of the same AI leaders gathered for a state dinner for Chinese President Xi Jinping.

Elon Musk of Tesla ( TSLA ), Jensen Huang of Nvidia ( NVDA ), and Lisa Su of Advanced Micro Devices ( AMD ) were all at the head table with Xi last Thursday and again received prominent spots near Trump.

After the meeting, Trump also said he was "very close" to a decision on an AI czar and would announce it in the next three to four days.

Other notable guests included Google ( GOOGL , GOOG ) CEO Sundar Pichai, Microsoft ( MSFT ) CEO Satya Nadella, OpenAI ( OPAI.PVT ) president Greg Brockman, Palantir ( PLTR ) CEO Alex Karp, Amazon ( AMZN ) founder Jeff Bezos, and others.

articles.title: US consumer confidence hits its lowest level since 2014 ahead of midterms
articles.summary: Rising goods and fuel costs are cited as key factors in the sharp drop in consumer confidence.
articles.body:
United States consumer confidence has fallen to its lowest level since 2014, just over one month before the congressional midterm elections.

Consumers pointed to higher costs for goods and services as the primary reason for the decline, according to The Conference Board, which released its monthly report on Tuesday.

“The Consumer Confidence Index deteriorated notably in September, following two prior months of softening,” Dana M Peterson, chief economist at The Conference Board, said in a release announcing the report.

Consumers pointed to higher prices at the pump as one of the driving factors. The average price for a gallon (3.78 litres) of petrol has jumped 37 cents over the past month, according to the American Automobile Association (AAA), which tracks daily petrol prices. The average price stood at $4.45 on Tuesday, compared with $4.08 a month ago.

“Oil and gas prices in particular rose to new heights, reflecting September’s surge in fuel costs. Comments about war/conflict eased this month but remained elevated,” Peterson said.

The consumer confidence report comes a day ahead of a key inflation report that the Federal Reserve uses to gauge the state of inflation, the personal consumption expenditures (PCE) index, which was up 3.7 percent in June from a year earlier.

The US central bank raised interest rates for the first time in three years earlier this month, driving up costs of credit cards and car and bank loans. It is set to make another decision on interest rates at its October 27-28 meeting, putting pressure on Republicans as consumer sentiment tumbles across political affiliations.

Consumer confidence fell among all political affiliations, according to the report, the second-to-last major consumer confidence reading before the midterm elections, which will determine the balance of power in Washington, DC.

US consumers think the Democratic Party would handle the economy better than their Republican counterparts, with 42 percent saying Democrats would do a better job compared with 34 percent for Republicans, according to a recent Marist poll.

US markets are only slightly lower as the trading day comes to a close. The tech-heavy Nasdaq closed down 0.08 percent, the Dow Jones Industrial Average declined 0.2 percent and the S&P 500 was down 0.1 percent.

US consumer sentiment fell to its lowest level since 2014 , new data showed, as unexpectedly weak jobs figures and elevated energy prices rekindled Republicans' midterm fears.

The White House has tried to staunch economic bleeding ahead of November through bond buybacks, promises of $5,000 checks, and — amid record fuel prices — a proposed diesel export ban.

articles.title: Decline in tourism hits US economy
articles.summary: Overseas visitors to the US are on track to drop by almost two million year-on-year.
articles.body:
Overseas visitors to the US are on track to drop by almost two million year-on-year, with even the FIFA Men's World Cup failing to arrest the decline in tourism.

The slide is hurting the US economy, and as Axios put it, is partly " self-inflicted :" There has been a significant drop in visitors from US allies like Canada and several European countries , which have been a target of Washington's trade war and taunts.

Meanwhile, China is attracting more visitors with its visa-free entry policies, and Japan's weak currency is drawing in a record number of tourists.

"We're the only major country in the world losing visitation," the head of the US Travel Association said. "It's mind-boggling."

articles.title: Robinhood is rolling out agentic AI trading accounts for the masses
articles.summary: Robinhood Markets is rolling out AI-agent-led trading accounts for everyday customers as it races to make autonomous trading a mainstream product for retail...
articles.body:
Robinhood Markets ( HOOD ) is rolling out AI-agent-led trading accounts for everyday customers as it races to make autonomous trading a mainstream product for retail investors.

The company said late Tuesday it will begin offering new so-called agentic accounts alongside other new products, including perpetual future contracts tied to crypto and options tied to earnings, as well as plans for weekend stock trading.

The product array is Robinhood's latest push to give retail investors increasingly sophisticated products "once reserved for hedge funds, big banks, and quant firms," CEO Vlad Tenev said in a press release ahead of the company's space-themed active trader event in Houston, Texas.

Robinhood will start releasing the new accounts to customers in a randomized manner over the coming weeks, while attendees at the Houston event — where Tenev appeared in an outfit reminiscent of Captain Kirk from Star Trek — received immediate access.

Robinhood first opened its trading platform to artificial intelligence in May by allowing customers to connect external AI agents to the online brokerage's trading infrastructure. Approximately 150,000 of its customers have since opened agentic accounts, the company said.

This latest version attempts to reduce the friction by moving the experience inside Robinhood's app.

"We were like, 'Oh, if we made this like 100 times easier and more delightful, … you could probably go from 150,000 people using it to millions," Abhishek Fatehpuria, Robinhood's vice president of product management, said in an interview.

Customers can instruct agents to monitor markets and execute trades, including through recurring strategies that run on pre-set conditions.

Trade-by-trade approval is switched on by default, but customers have the ability to turn approval off, allowing an agent to trade autonomously. Agents can only use funds transferred into a separate agentic account.

Robinhood will initially offer customers access to models created by Anthropic and OpenAI ( OPAI.PVT ).

The company will bill customers for model usage through its platform and said one OpenAI model, Luna, will be free for the remainder of 2026. The company declined to disclose whether it has revenue-sharing arrangements with AI providers.

Robinhood will begin rolling out the new accounts to customers on a randomized basis over the coming weeks, while attendees at the Houston event will receive immediate access.

Customers are responsible for their agents' trades, Robinhood said, adding that it hasn't yet measured or compared the investment outcomes of customers using agentic accounts with those of other non-agentic strategies.

articles.title: What products are part of US-China $60 billion tariff cuts deal
articles.summary: The U.S. and Chinese governments unveiled tariff cuts on Monday, affecting $60 billion worth of goods in varying markets. The list released by the White House spans the U.S. import of 77 categories of Chinese goods – including Christmas decorations, fireworks and children’s toys. The Chinese imports of U.S. goods, meanwhile, cover 1,619 categories of…
articles.body:
The U.S. and Chinese governments unveiled tariff cuts on Monday, affecting $60 billion worth of goods in varying markets.

The list released by the White House spans the U.S. import of 77 categories of Chinese goods – including Christmas decorations, fireworks and children’s toys. The Chinese imports of U.S. goods , meanwhile, cover 1,619 categories of products that are various American agricultural products.

The 30-30 framework impacts $30 billion worth of goods from each country and marks another step for the U.S. in reducing its tariff deficit against China.

The U.S. import focus remains on consumer goods as concern over inflation and rising gas prices continues to grow. The Conference Board reported on Tuesday that the consumer confidence index fell to 81.9 in September, down 6.7 points from August. That marked the lowest point for the metric since 2014, when consumer sentiment was rebounding from a low point of less than 30 during the financial crisis.

The Chinese import focus, meanwhile, also concerned U.S. agricultural products, notably soybeans and related products. The American Soybean Association said in a statement the product was critical for tariff negotiations as China has shown a continued commitment to purchase a minimum of 25 million metric tons of U.S. soybeans annually in the years 2026, 2027 and 2028.

“China remains an important market for U.S. soybeans, and we want to see a strong trading relationship that allows more customers in China to purchase our soybeans,” ASA President and Ohio soybean farmer Scott Metzger said.

Microchips, electronics and semiconductors were notably not included or covered under the agreement.

A group of Senate Democrats demanded President Trump to close loopholes that allow China to subvert U.S. export bans on semiconductors and microchips – saying the technology helps China build “dangerous AI systems.”

“China is accelerating its drive for AI dominance by exploiting weaknesses in the administration’s export controls to access advanced chips and manufacturing equipment,” they wrote.

articles.title: 5 hurdles facing Noel Tata and an unlisted Tata Sons
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Noel Tata’s plan to keep Tata Sons private faces five hurdles, the steepest of which is a Reserve Bank of India (RBI) that has already refused to
articles.body: MUMBAI: Noel Tata’s plan to keep Tata Sons private faces five hurdles, the steepest of which is a Reserve Bank of India (RBI) that has already refused to release the group’s holding company from its rules. The chairman of Tata Trusts has proposed merging Tata Electronics Systems Solutions and Tata Consulting Engineers into Tata Sons, a move designed to take the holding company outside the RBI’s upper-layer NBFC and Core Investment Company regulations, and so avoid a public listing. Success depends on winning over his own trustees, a divided Tata Sons board, the central bank, an aggrieved minority shareholder and a 75% vote he cannot yet count on.Tata TrustsDissent persists at home. Noel emailed the merger proposal to trustees Monday in his capacity as chairman of Tata Trusts, relying on a July 28, 2025 resolution. But some trustees said the resolution empowered N Chandrasekaran, chairman of Tata Sons, not Noel, to keep Tata Sons unlisted and to engage with the RBI. They added that no board meeting was held to weigh the proposal before it was unveiled. They also questioned whether the Tata Sons board can consider the plan without approval from both the Sir Dorabji Tata Trust and the Sir Ratan Tata Trust (SRTT), the latter currently under a regulatory restriction.The Tata Sons boardThe board is split 5:1, and the majority sees a listing as the simplest route to compliance. Noel can seek a board meeting to consider the plan, but he needs the backing of fellow Trusts nominee director Venu Srinivasan. On Noel’s reading of Article 121 of Tata Sons’ Articles of Association, the merger fails if one Trusts nominee votes against. By Tata Sons’ reading, if the Trusts’ nominees vote in different directions, the result would be a split and Chandrasekaran would have the chairman’s casting vote. Srinivasan had backed Chandrasekaran’s reappointment; only Noel had opposed. Add the majority view that an IPO offers greater regulatory certainty than a restructuring, and the outcome looks stacked against Noel.Reserve Bank’s NOCThe regulator is the most formidable obstacle. Earlier this month it rejected Tata Sons’ application to surrender its CIC registration, even though the company had repaid more than Rs 30,000 crore of debt. That keeps alive the requirement to comply with the upper-layer NBFC-CIC rules including listing. The merger is designed to ensure Tata Sons no longer qualifies as an NBFC or a CIC, but the RBI’s 2025 NBFC-voluntary amalgamations directions require an explicit no-objection certificate (NOC) for the proposal as part of the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) approval process. The RBI is also likely to weigh longer-term prospects: if the merged businesses are later demerged to attract outside investment or an IPO, Tata Sons would revert to NBFC-CIC status.Shapoorji Pallonji GroupThe largest minority shareholder in Tata Sons, the Shapoorji Pallonji (SP) Group, has long advocated a listing to unlock value. Scrapping the prospect of an IPO could prompt SP to challenge the restructuring before the NCLT as oppressive to them.Tata Cos’ vote might be keyThe Trusts collectively own 66% of Tata Sons, but SRTT with 24% cannot currently vote on the merger because of the regulatory restriction. That makes Tata companies, which hold 13%, pivotal as the resolution requires 75% of shareholders to approve it. Their stance is unclear, and they are led by Chandrasekaran. If Tata companies and SP, which holds an 18% stake, both vote against, the restructuring resolution fails.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Trump’s ads have cost taxpayers at least $2.5 million, with funding from Customs and Border Protection
articles.summary: Millions of taxpayer dollars have already been spent on President Donald Trump’s hagiographic ads, according to estimates by a leading political ad-tracking firm. And a total of $20 million has been allocated for the effort, which watchdog groups have deemed illegal.
articles.body: Millions of taxpayer dollars have already been spent on President Donald Trump’s hagiographic ads, according to estimates by a leading political ad-tracking firm. And a total of $20 million has been allocated for the effort, which watchdog groups have deemed illegal. The TV airtime for the three different Trump ads has cost at least $2.5 million to date, the ad-tracking firm AdImpact told CNN. The actual cost of the taxpayer-funded ad campaign is even higher, but can’t be fully ascertained. The money for these ads is coming from Customs and Border Protection, or CBP for short, two sources familiar with the matter told CNN. Earlier this month, the White House Office of Management and Budget, led by Russell Vought, allocated $20 million to CBP for what it called “OBBBA commemorative events.” (OBBBA is an abbreviation for the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, which Trump signed into law in 2025.) Shortly after the $20 million was allocated, CBP contracted an advertising company, LMD Agency Inc., for a national media campaign in the same dollar amount. Days later, the ads began to appear on national television, two additional sources told CNN. LMD’s parent company, MarCom Group, did not respond to CNN’s request for comment. CBP is an agency within the Department of Homeland Security. On Tuesday, two Democratic senators, Patty Murray and Chris Murphy, sent a letter to Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin accusing the department of “a shockingly corrupt misuse of taxpayer dollars.” The propagandistic ads also faced a fresh challenge from the government watchdog group Public Citizen on Tuesday. The ads “appear to violate the federal law against using taxpayer funds to finance propaganda and related provisions of the appropriations laws as well as the Hatch Act,” Public Citizen co-presidents Robert Weissman and Lisa Gilbert and the group’s lobbyist, Craig Holman, wrote in a complaint to the Federal Communications Commission and the Federal Trade Commission. It’s unclear whether any outside groups have the legal standing to sue the Trump administration over the ads. And while lawmakers on both sides of the aisle have questioned their legality, Republicans — who currently control both the House and the Senate — have not acted. Following the taxpayer money AdImpact’s analysis for CNN found 2,766 total ad airings between September 23 and 29. The ads have aired on Fox News and the big four broadcast networks. About 30% of the ad spend has been dedicated to NFL and college football games, according to the firm’s research. The ads have also appeared during shows like ABC’s “The View,” CBS’s “Elsbeth” and NBC’s “The Weakest Link.” Because the spots have been classified as a “public service announcement” rather than a traditional political ad buy, the exact spending is not publicly disclosed or verifiable. AdImpact’s estimates are based on air dates, times, local markets, and other factors. The firm said the first Trump ad to air, featuring the song “Love Me” by JMSN, has aired on more than 1,300 occasions so far. Lawyers for JMSN sent a cease-and-desist letter to the White House earlier this week, demanding that the administration no longer use the song. The text “Paid for by the US Government” is seen on screen at the end of each of the three ads, including one repurposed version of an ad from Trump’s 2024 presidential campaign. The “paid for” disclosure conflicts with the administration’s insistence that the ads are “public service announcements” akin to those that past administrations have aired about Medicare, Obamacare and Covid-19 vaccinations. For actual public service announcements, the TV airtime is usually donated. Public Citizen argued in its FCC and FTC complaint that the Trump ads “do not refer to any specific governmental program and they do not serve the purpose of informing the public about any specific governmental program.” The ads were created in-house by the White House video team, two Trump advisers told CNN, and were personally driven by the president, who was involved in the selection of imagery and videos used, according to a separate source. The Wall Street Journal first reported where the money came from. Who will enforce the rules? On Tuesday, Public Citizen warned that TV stations could theoretically lose their broadcast licenses for knowingly airing the ads. “A station knowingly broadcasting illegal, taxpayer-funded partisan propaganda has failed its public interest mandate, forming the basis of a formal license renewal challenge,” they wrote. The track record of Trump’s FCC, however, shows the agency won’t try to penalize a station for running pro-Trump content. Instead, the agency has challenged ABC’s licenses, a move that many observers have linked to the network’s support for programs like “Jimmy Kimmel Live!” that are harshly critical of the president. Public Citizen also filed a separate complaint Monday with the Government Accountability Office, the nonpartisan agency typically tasked with investigating this type of issue, as well as the US Office of the Special Counsel, calling for an investigation “into who produced these ads and at what cost to taxpayers.” What constitutes illegal government propaganda, and who can be held accountable for it, is less straightforward. Propaganda hasn’t been defined in US law, but the Government Accountability Office has identified three categories, including “self-aggrandizement” or “puffery.” “The most immediate check on this kind of behavior is supposed to be and needs to be Congress. Congress has not asserted itself as the first branch of government with the power of the purse to hold the president accountable,” said Donald Sherman, president and CEO of Citizens for Responsibility and Ethics, or CREW. GOP lawmakers may be hesitant to provide accountability, he added, because the ads “are designed to boost Republicans in Congress.” And Hatch Act violations — government officials engaging in partisan political activity while on duty — have largely been dismissed in recent years. Trump administration officials in his first term were alleged to have repeatedly violated the Hatch Act with no penalty. The same was alleged during the Biden administration. Public Citizen said in a previous statement that it has filed dozens of complaints with the administration about Hatch Act violations, but thinks they have been ignored.

articles.title: Apple Will Sell 6 Million iPhone Duos in 2026, Counterpoint Says
articles.summary: Apple Inc. is set to sell about 6 million units of the iPhone Duo this year, Counterpoint Research said, offering the first estimate for how the company’s in...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Apple Inc. is set to sell about 6 million units of the iPhone Duo this year, Counterpoint Research said, offering the first estimate for how the company's inaugural foldable device will fare.

The figure, more typical of the niche foldable segment than Apple's usual smartphone sales, is contingent on how well the company ramps up production of the new hardware, Counterpoint senior analyst Ivan Lam said. Priced at $1,999 and set for an October release, the iPhone Duo sits atop the Apple lineup and carries industry-wide hopes for stoking greater interest and sales of foldables.

Market researcher IDC estimates foldables will grow 13% to 22.9 million units shipped this year with Apple's help. Without the iPhone Duo, the segment would have seen a decline, it said.

Introduced alongside the Duo this month, Apple's iPhone 18 Pro family has gotten off to a fast start in China, Counterpoint said. The company's Pro edition smartphones were for the first time released without a corresponding base-model upgrade, steering consumers looking for an upgrade to the pricier models and helping deliver a 12% rise compared to the iPhone 17 Pro's initial sales. That performance bucked a broad downtrend in the world's largest smartphone market, with Chinese brands taking the brunt of a 17% year-on-year decline across this summer, according to the researchers.

That helped Apple grab 33% of China's highly competitive smartphone arena, an unusual feat when companies like Huawei Technologies Co., Oppo, Vivo and Xiaomi Corp. usually have roughly equal shares with Apple. But elevated component costs are forcing all phone makers to raise prices and try to make up the shortfall of unit sales in higher revenue per unit. That works in Apple's favor by narrowing the cost advantage of its rivals.

"Price hikes of over $200 on many Chinese flagship models may have raised the price anchor, strengthening the iPhone's relative value proposition," Lam said.

articles.title: Apple Pay finally launches in India after years on the sidelines
articles.summary: Some of India's largest banks are holding off on supporting Apple Pay initially.
articles.body:
Apple began rolling out Apple Pay in India on Tuesday, as TechCrunch was first to report. Its first banking partner is Axis Bank, the country's third-largest private-sector lender. The move brings the company's payments service to the world's most populous country after years of delays in a market dominated by the state-backed United Payments Interface (UPI).

The initial rollout is limited. Apple Pay supports eligible Axis Bank cards on Visa and Mastercard, but not India's homegrown RuPay network. Acceptance will also be restricted to merchants and payment terminals that have been enabled for the service.

Unlike India's ubiquitous Unified Payments Interface (UPI) system, which lets consumers make instant bank-to-bank payments without relying on cards, Apple Pay is card-based and requires individual issuers and payment infrastructure providers to integrate with the service. This makes a broad rollout more complex. Apple's commercial terms have also emerged as a sticking point with some of India's largest banks, the people said.

Apple is seeking a fee of about 20 basis points (0.2%) on transactions, according to the people, a significant bite out of the roughly 40 to 50 basis points (0.4% to 0.5%) of margin in the payments layer. The fee structure is broadly consistent with Apple Pay's commercial model in other markets, the people said. HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, and SBI Card are not supporting Apple Pay at launch as negotiations over commercial terms continue, one of the people told TechCrunch.

Apple, Axis Bank, HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, and SBI Card did not respond to requests for comment on the launch. Earlier this month, Reuters reported that Apple was preparing to launch Apple Pay in India in October, starting with Axis Bank credit cards.

Apple Pay has entered a payments market that looks markedly different from the U.S. and other card-heavy economies. India's digital payments boom has been driven largely by UPI, the state-backed system that lets consumers move money directly between bank accounts.

UPI handles the bulk of digital payments in India, where scanning a QR code to pay directly from a bank account has become commonplace. Apple Pay, by contrast, initially addresses a much smaller card payments market.

Nevertheless, Apple Pay could appeal to India's growing base of iPhone users, who tend to be more affluent and are more likely to use premium credit cards. Those customers could make the service hard for banks to ignore, despite UPI's dominance.

Even if Apple Pay remains a niche service, the economics could still make India meaningful for Apple. The transaction fee the iPhone maker would charge would give it another way to monetize its growing base of iPhone users in the country, the people said.

articles.title: Son claimed share in mother’s Delhi house, saying he paid Rs 1.5 lakh for land and Rs 60,000 for construction; Delhi High Court rejects claim, orders him and wife to vacate
articles.summary: Your husband buys a property in your name. Does that give your son an automatic right to co-ownership by staying there?
articles.body: Your husband buys a property in your name. Does that give your son an automatic right to co-ownership by staying there? What if the son claims to have spent money on construction?In one such case, the Delhi High Court recently directed a son and his wife, residents of Karawal Nagar, to vacate his parents' house and remove any locks they had placed on the property.The case involved a son who continued living in his mother's house after his marriage despite having no independent title over the property. His mother, meanwhile, relied on a General Power of Attorney (GPA), an Agreement to Sale and a Will as documents establishing her ownership of the house.What the case is aboutThe woman had been living in the property since it was purchased in 1996. The house was purchased in the woman’s name by her late husband, who was employed and used his savings to acquire the property. The transaction was supported by a General Power of Attorney (GPA), Agreement to Sell, Will and Receipt, all dated November 1, 1996.After he got married, the woman allowed her son and daughter-in-law to stay in the property because of their family relationship. According to her case, however, allowing them to live there did not give the son any ownership or independent right, title or interest in the house. The property continued to belong exclusively to her.The woman said she occupied the ground floor, where she had access to one room, a kitchen and a shop. Her son, meanwhile, was in possession of another room on the ground floor as well as one room and a kitchen on the first floor. Over time, relations between the woman and the couple deteriorated. She alleged that her son and his wife fought with her and subjected her to harassment.Following these incidents, she decided to sever her relationship with her son and daughter-in-law and asked them to leave the property. The son and his wife, however, locked the rooms that were in their possession before leaving the house, according to the woman.She subsequently alleged that her son and his wife joined together and devised a fraudulent plan to take control of the property. She claimed that they prepared forged and fabricated documents that purported to transfer the property in her son’s name for a consideration of Rs 1.5 lakh.According to the woman, he made an apparent error in the documents because the date mentioned was January 12, 2003, which was a Sunday, when courts are generally closed.She further alleged that her son’s actions continued years later. She claimed that on July 2, 2013, he obtained a signed cheque and withdrew Rs 50,000 from her late husband's bank account. This further strained the relationship between mother and son. In August 2013, she consequently lodged a complaint against her son at the police station.The dispute also extended to the property's electricity connection. On October 4, 2013, she submitted a written complaint to BSES Yamuna Power after learning that her son had applied for an independent electricity connection without informing her. Since she claimed ownership of the house, she objected to the application and said she was aggrieved by his action.After the complaint to BSES Yamuna Power, her son challenged his mother in court by filing Civil Suit No. 219/2013. The court dismissed the suit on November 18, 2015.She subsequently approached the court on January 25, 2016, seeking recovery of her property from her son. She succeeded in the case on September 8, 2026.Why the woman won the case against her son?The son put forward several grounds to claim a share in the property. He argued that his father's salary was too low to afford the purchase of the house. He said that, at the time, he was working as an electrician and had contributed Rs 1.5 lakh towards the purchase of the land.He further claimed that he paid another Rs 60,000 when the house was constructed. On the basis of these alleged contributions, the son told the Delhi High Court that he should be treated as a joint owner of the property.However, the son did not produce evidence to establish that he had made either of these payments.The Delhi High Court said: “Even otherwise, mere contribution towards household expenses, construction or repairs of a property cannot, by itself, does not confer any right of co-ownership.”He also failed to demonstrate that he independently held any title to the property. In contrast, his mother had documents supporting her ownership, including the Will, GPA and Agreement to Sale.The Delhi High Court referred to the recent judgment in Suraj Lamp & Industries (P) Ltd. v. State of Haryana, which held that a transaction involving an Agreement to Sale, GPA and Will does not, by itself, transfer absolute ownership of an immovable property.However, the court noted that in this case, the son himself was relying on his mother's title to the property.The Delhi High Court also examined the argument concerning the fact that the property had been purchased with money paid by the woman’s husband but was held in her name. The court said that this fact alone would not make the property benami.The Delhi High Court explained that under clause (iii), a property is not treated as benami when it is held by an individual in the name of his spouse or child and the consideration for the property has been provided or paid from the known sources of that individual.On the basis of this legal position, the Delhi High Court held that the fact that the husband had paid the sale consideration did not, by itself, give the son any right in the property.Advocate Shourya Garg told ET that the son’s own admission that his father had purchased the property in 1996, despite the property being registered in his mother's name, became significant in the case.Garg said: "The son admitted that his father had bought the property back in 1996, even though it was registered in his mother's name. That single admission ended up costing him the case, because you cannot accept your father's role in a purchase and then also argue that the purchase itself does not hold up legally. Those two positions cancel each other out. Once he took that stand, the court did not even need to weigh in on the bigger Suraj Lamps precedent that usually comes up in these benami-adjacent disputes."Garg says: "This ruling means the son and his wife have to vacate the property."You use AI every day.
